message.content:
# Finding ∫ exp(x)\*cos(x) dx

## Integration by Parts (First Application)

Let I = ∫ exp(x)\*cos(x) dx

Choose:
- u = cos(x) → du = -sin(x) dx
- dv = exp(x) dx → v = exp(x)

Applying the formula ∫u dv = uv - ∫v du:

I = exp(x)\*cos(x) - ∫exp(x)\*(-sin(x)) dx
I = exp(x)\*cos(x) + ∫exp(x)\*sin(x) dx  --- (1)

## Integration by Parts (Second Application)

Now evaluate J = ∫exp(x)\*sin(x) dx

Choose:
- u = sin(x) → du = cos(x) dx
- dv = exp(x) dx → v = exp(x)

J = exp(x)\*sin(x) - ∫exp(x)\*cos(x) dx
J = exp(x)\*sin(x) - I  --- (2)

## Solving for I

Substituting (2) into (1):

I = exp(x)\*cos(x) + exp(x)\*sin(x) - I

2\*I = exp(x)\*cos(x) + exp(x)\*sin(x)

I = (exp(x)\*cos(x) + exp(x)\*sin(x)) / 2 + C

## Verification

d/dx [(exp(x)\*cos(x) + exp(x)\*sin(x))/2]
= (1/2)\*[exp(x)\*cos(x) - exp(x)\*sin(x) + exp(x)\*sin(x) + exp(x)\*cos(x)]
= (1/2)\*[2\*exp(x)\*cos(x)]
= exp(x)\*cos(x) ✓

<answer>(exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x))/2 + C</answer>

Let I = ∫exp(x)*cos(x) dx

Using integration by parts: ∫u dv = uv - ∫v du

Let u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
Then du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

I = exp(x)*cos(x) - ∫exp(x)*(-sin(x)) dx

Now I need to find ∫exp(x)*sin(x) dx. Let's call this J.

J = ∫exp(x)*sin(x) dx

Using integration by parts again:
Let u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
Then du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

J = exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫exp(x)*cos(x) dx
J = exp(x)*sin(x) - I

So going back:
I = exp(x)*cos(x) + J
I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) - I
2I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x)

So the answer is: (exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x))/2 + C

= (1/2)[exp(x)*cos(x) - exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x)]
